subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Transport in which small particles bounce along the river bed is called:
questions.explain: Saltation is the bouncing or hopping of small particles along the bed.

questions.q: Natural raised banks of sediment along the edges of a river channel are called:
questions.explain: Levees are raised banks built up by repeated deposition during floods.

questions.q: A wave-cut platform is formed as:
options: Sediment is deposited at a river mouth
A stack collapses into a stump
A cliff retreats, leaving a rocky surface at its base
questions.explain: As waves undercut and the cliff retreats, a flat rocky platform is left at the base.

questions.q: The boundary separating one drainage basin from another is the:
questions.explain: The watershed is the ridge of high land marking the edge of a drainage basin.

questions.q: Longshore drift is the process that:
options: Transports sediment ALONG the coast in a zig-zag motion
questions.explain: Longshore drift moves sediment along the coast as swash arrives at an angle and backwash returns straight down.

questions.q: On a coast with alternating hard and soft rock, resistant rock tends to form ____ and softer rock forms ____.
questions.explain: Resistant rock juts out as headlands while softer rock is eroded back into bays.

questions.q: The coastal erosion process where waves throw pebbles against a cliff, wearing it away, is:
questions.explain: Abrasion occurs as waves hurl sediment against the cliff, grinding it away.

questions.q: A delta forms where a river:
options: Deposits its load as it enters a sea or lake
Begins at its source on a mountain
questions.explain: Deltas form where a river deposits sediment as it slows on entering still water.

questions.q: Which of these is HARD engineering coastal defence?
questions.explain: A sea wall is a hard engineering structure that reflects wave energy.

questions.q: A waterfall and its plunge pool are typically formed where the river crosses:
options: A band of soft rock over hard rock
A band of hard rock over softer rock
questions.explain: Soft rock beneath a hard cap is eroded faster, forming a waterfall and plunge pool.

questions.q: Which is an example of SOFT engineering flood management?
questions.explain: Soft engineering, like planting trees and zoning land use, works with natural processes.

options: Have a strong backwash that removes material and erodes the coast
questions.explain: Destructive waves have a strong backwash and steep, frequent form, eroding the coast.
